description: Main Stage presentations and live Q&A sessions at DEF CON Safe Mode, covering wireless combo chip escalation, Ripple20 supply chain vulnerabilities, ATM jackpotting, macOS malware, and cloud privilege escalation.

talks.title: Beyond Root: Custom Firmware for Embedded Mobile Chipsets
talks.teaser: Christopher Wade reverse engineers closed proprietary NFC controllers in modern smartphones, patching microcontroller firmware to expand RF capabilities.
talks.summary:
The Hidden Closed Hardware in Rooted Smartphones

While rooting Android smartphones grants root privileges over the Linux kernel and userland, specialized embedded coprocessors remain closed and inaccessible.

Reverse Engineering Smartphone NFC Controllers

Christopher Wade examines proprietary NFC microcontrollers deployed across modern handsets, analyzing hardware interfaces and proprietary bootloader firmware.

Patching Firmware and Bypassing Silicon Protections

By overcoming memory readout protections and patching firmware binaries, researchers can bypass silicon restrictions and manipulate raw RF modulation.

Unlocking Advanced Wireless Capabilities

Custom controller firmware enables arbitrary frame transmission, custom tag emulation, and low-level protocol fuzzing directly from commodity smartphone hardware.

talks.title: Spectra: New Wireless Escalation Targets
talks.teaser: Jiska Classen and Francesco Gringoli disclose 'Spectra', breaking hardware coexistence isolation in Broadcom and Cypress Wi-Fi/Bluetooth combo chips.
talks.summary:
Wireless Coexistence in Modern Mobile Silicon

To conserve board space and share 2.4 GHz antennas, smartphones and laptops combine Wi-Fi and Bluetooth into single combo chips with shared RAM and internal buses.

Deconstructing Broadcom and Cypress Coexistence Architectures

Jiska Classen and Francesco Gringoli analyze on-chip coexistence protocols, reverse engineering proprietary arbitration logic and shared hardware memory structures.

Lateral Movement Across Wireless Cores

Exploiting coexistence vulnerabilities allows an attacker who compromises the Wi-Fi core over the air to jump directly into the Bluetooth core, establishing stealthy persistence.

Extracting Keystrokes and Hardening Firmware

The researchers demonstrate over-the-air Bluetooth keystroke injection and coordinate security mitigations with silicon manufacturers.

talks.title: Only Takes a Spark: Popping a Shell on 1000 Nodes
talks.teaser: ayoul3 details attacking Apache Spark big data clusters, demonstrating how misconfigurations and unauthenticated APIs yield root shells across thousands of nodes.
talks.summary:
Apache Spark in Distributed Data Processing

Apache Spark powers enterprise data pipelines, machine learning workloads, and analytics clusters spanning hundreds or thousands of high-performance compute nodes.

Exposed Cluster Management Interfaces

ayoul3 evaluates default configurations and unauthenticated master/worker REST APIs frequently exposed across corporate networks and public clouds.

Executing Arbitrary Code Across 1000 Nodes

Submitting malicious job payloads and manipulating deserialization endpoints enables executing arbitrary operating system commands simultaneously across entire cluster nodes.

Defending Distributed Big Data Infrastructure

The author outlines essential security controls, including enabling mutual TLS authentication, configuring network ACLs, and isolating worker processes.

talks.title: Bypassing Biometric Systems with 3D Printing
talks.teaser: Yamila Levalle explores spoofing biometric fingerprint and facial recognition sensors on consumer smartphones using low-cost 3D printing and conductive materials.
talks.summary:
The Rapid Proliferation of Biometric Authentication

Biometric authentication has replaced passwords across billions of smartphones and physical access control readers under the assumption of unforgeable physical identity.

3D Modeling Latent Fingerprints and Facial Topology

Yamila Levalle demonstrates extracting latent fingerprints from physical surfaces and photos, reconstructing precise 3D relief models using CAD software.

Fabricating Conductive Spoofs with Budget 3D Printers

Using consumer resin 3D printers and conductive silicones/materials, Levalle fabricates synthetic finger prosthetics capable of mimicking human skin capacitance and ridges.

Defeating Optical and Capacitive Sensors

Experimental testing demonstrates successful bypasses across leading smartphone sensors, urging hardware vendors to integrate robust liveness detection algorithms.

talks.title: Detecting Fake 4G Base Stations in Real Time
talks.teaser: EFF researcher Cooper Quintin introduces Crocodile Hunter, an open-source tool using low-cost SDRs to detect 4G LTE IMSI catchers (Hailstorm) in real time.
talks.summary:
The Evolution from 2G to 4G IMSI Catchers

While early cell-site simulators (Stingrays) forced devices to unencrypted 2G networks, modern surveillance devices (such as Hailstorm) operate directly on 4G LTE protocols.

Understanding 4G Cell-Site Simulator Mechanics

Cooper Quintin explains how 4G IMSI catchers manipulate LTE broadcast parameters and Tracking Area Updates (TAUs) to intercept device identifiers and location data.

Introducing Crocodile Hunter for Real-Time Detection

Quintin presents Crocodile Hunter, an open-source monitoring framework combining software-defined radios (SDRs) and GPS to identify rogue base station anomalies.

Mapping and Auditing Cellular Surveillance

Demonstrating live drive-by spectrum monitoring shows how civil society groups can map unauthorized cell-site simulator deployments and protect protest environments.

talks.title: Lateral Movement & Privilege Escalation in GCP
talks.teaser: Dylan Ayrey and Allison Donovan dissect Google Cloud Platform's security model, exploiting default service account permissions and `actAs` delegation to escalate privileges.
talks.summary:
Contrasting GCP and AWS Cloud Security Architectures

While AWS enforces explicit least-privilege defaults, Google Cloud Platform (GCP) frequently assigns powerful default service accounts to managed compute instances, Cloud Functions, and Jupyter notebooks.

Abusing the `actAs` IAM Permission

Dylan Ayrey and Allison Donovan analyze the mechanics of `iam.serviceAccounts.actAs`, illustrating how unprivileged identities can impersonate high-privilege service accounts.

Chaining GCP Services for Full Organization Compromise

The researchers demonstrate novel lateral movement paths through Cloud Build, Compute Engine, and Cloud Storage to escalate privileges to Organization Administrator.

Hardening IAM Policies and Least Privilege

Actionable recommendations provide cloud architects with automated auditing scripts to eliminate dangerous default service account roles and enforce fine-grained IAM conditions.

talks.title: Domain Fronting is Dead, Long Live Domain Fronting: Using TLS 1.3
talks.teaser: Erik Hunstad resurrects domain fronting using TLS 1.3 Encrypted Server Name Indication (ESNI/ECH), bypassing modern network censorship and deep packet inspection.
talks.summary:
The Demise of Classic Domain Fronting

Domain fronting allowed circumvention tools and red teams to conceal HTTPS destinations by mismatched HTTP Host headers, until major CDN providers disabled the technique in 2018.

Enter TLS 1.3 and Encrypted SNI (ESNI)

Erik Hunstad introduces next-generation domain fronting leveraging TLS 1.3 and Encrypted Server Name Indication (ESNI/ECH) to encrypt the TLS handshake SNI extension.

Fooling Modern Deep Packet Inspection Engines

By decoupling public DNS records, frontend CDN endpoints, and encrypted backend server names, traffic appears completely indistinguishable from benign HTTPS traffic.

Tool Release and Circumvention Strategies

Hunstad releases proof-of-concept tooling, demonstrating how human rights activists and privacy tools can maintain resilient connectivity across censored networks.

talks.title: Getting Shells on z/OS with Surrogat Chains
talks.teaser: Jake Labelle demonstrates automated privilege escalation on IBM z/OS mainframes by discovering and chaining complex RACF SURROGAT class permissions to gain root.
talks.summary:
Mainframe Security Architecture and the SURROGAT Class

IBM z/OS enterprise mainframes rely on Resource Access Control Facility (RACF) security databases, where the SURROGAT class permits submitting batch jobs as another user without a password.

The Emergence of Implicit Permission Chains

In legacy mainframe environments spanning decades and hundreds of thousands of accounts, nested job delegation rules inadvertently create complex privilege elevation graphs.

Automating Graph Analysis to Discover Root Paths

Jake Labelle introduces automated graph analysis tooling that maps out multi-step user-to-user SURROGAT chains leading directly to SPECIAL (mainframe root) privileges.

Auditing and Remediating RACF Configurations

The presentation provides mainframe system programmers with auditing scripts to identify circular delegations and enforce strict batch job submission controls.

talks.title: Office Drama on macOS
talks.teaser: Patrick Wardle analyzes emerging macOS macro-based Office malware campaigns, dissecting Apple sandbox escapes and synthetic click persistence tricks.
talks.summary:
The Rise of Macro-Based Attacks on macOS

While Microsoft Office VBA macro attacks have targeted Windows for decades, adversary groups increasingly deploy weaponized Word and Excel documents targeting macOS enterprise workstations.

Deconstructing Real-World macOS Macro Payloads

Patrick Wardle analyzes recent nation-state and cybercrime documents, examining how malicious VBA code invokes Python, Bash, and native Objective-C APIs via MacScript.

Bypassing the Apple App Sandbox

Wardle uncovers vulnerabilities in macOS Office sandboxing, demonstrating how attackers escape sandbox constraints, write persistent login launch items, and access sensitive files.

Detection Engineering and Endpoint Defenses

The author releases open-source heuristic monitoring tools, providing macOS defenders with behavioral rules to detect malicious Office child process spawning.

talks.title: Abusing P2P to Hack 3 Million Cameras
talks.teaser: Paul Marrapese exposes critical vulnerabilities in the iSmartViewPro P2P protocol, enabling unauthenticated remote hijacking of over 3 million IoT cameras globally.
talks.summary:
The Insecurity of Plug-and-Play IoT P2P Cloud Networks

To facilitate easy remote smartphone access without port forwarding, millions of low-cost IP cameras ship with enabled-by-default Peer-to-Peer (P2P) cloud tunneling protocols.

Reverse Engineering the CS2 Network and iSmartViewPro

Paul Marrapese reverse engineers proprietary UDP-based P2P protocols used by Chinese OEM white-label vendors, mapping out central directory servers and client handshakes.

Unauthenticated Remote Hijacking and MitM Attacks

Flaws in device serial number authentication and unencrypted UDP traffic allow remote attackers to intercept live video feeds, steal credentials, and execute arbitrary commands.

The Challenges of Disclosing Flaws in White-Label Hardware

Marrapese highlights the systemic difficulty of coordinating patches across hundreds of re-branded white-label consumer hardware manufacturers.

talks.title: Don't Be Silly It's Only a Lightbulb: Hacking Smart Lighting
talks.teaser: Eyal Itkin exploits Zigbee radio firmware in Philips Hue smart lightbulbs to trigger a bridge buffer overflow, pivoting from smart lights into internal corporate networks.
talks.summary:
Smart Lightbulbs as Network Infiltration Vectors

While smart lightbulbs are often dismissed as harmless IoT gadgets, their integration into home and corporate Wi-Fi bridges makes them prime initial access targets.

Reverse Engineering the Zigbee Light Link Protocol

Eyal Itkin analyzes the wireless Zigbee protocol stack on Philips Hue hardware, evaluating how lighting bridges discover and control peripheral bulbs.

Triggering a Heap Overflow in the Hue Bridge

By manipulating Zigbee radio packets emitted from a compromised bulb, an attacker triggers a heap buffer overflow in the central Hue Bridge daemon, executing arbitrary code.

Pivoting from Lighting Silicon to Enterprise LANs

Demonstrating a complete lateral movement chain shows how an attacker parked outside a building can compromise a smart bulb and pivot onto internal corporate networks.

talks.title: Don't Ruck Us Again: The Exploit Returns
talks.teaser: Gal Zror discloses six new vulnerabilities in Ruckus Wireless ZoneDirector and Unleashed access points, achieving unauthenticated root RCE over the air.
talks.summary:
Revisiting Enterprise Wi-Fi Controller Security

Following earlier disclosures in enterprise wireless infrastructure, Gal Zror conducts a comprehensive follow-up audit of Ruckus Wireless ZoneDirector and Unleashed firmware.

Discovering Six New Critical Vulnerabilities

Zror reveals a chain of six distinct flaws—spanning command injection, information leakage, credential overwrites, stack buffer overflows, and stored XSS.

Unauthenticated Root Code Execution

Chaining pre-authentication web handler bugs allows an unauthenticated network attacker to overwrite administrative credentials and execute arbitrary root shellcode on access points.

Vendor Patch Analysis and Fleet Hardening

The author reviews vendor security patches, providing wireless network engineers with detection signatures to audit enterprise Wi-Fi deployments.

talks.title: Room for Escape: Scribbling Outside the Lines of Template Security
talks.teaser: Alvaro Muñoz and Oleksandr Mirosh uncover server-side template injection (SSTI) RCE vulnerabilities across leading enterprise Content Management Systems.
talks.summary:
Server-Side Template Engines in Enterprise CMS

Modern Content Management Systems (CMS) rely heavily on template engines (such as Freemarker, Velocity, and Twig) to dynamically render user-customized web content.

The Evolution of Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI)

Alvaro Muñoz and Oleksandr Mirosh explore the mechanics of SSTI, analyzing how template engines expose internal programming language reflection and class loaders.

Bypassing Template Sandboxes to Achieve RCE

Dissecting popular enterprise CMS platforms reveals novel sandbox bypass techniques, allowing attackers to invoke native operating system commands through template directives.

Hardening Template Engines and Defenses

The researchers release open-source security guidelines and secure configuration baselines for developers to sandbox template execution safely.

talks.title: Hacking Traffic Lights
talks.teaser: Wesley Neelen and Rik van Duijn reverse engineer smart traffic control systems in the Netherlands, spoofing cyclist priority apps to manipulate green lights at will.
talks.summary:
The Rise of Connected Smart City Infrastructure

Municipalities worldwide are modernizing urban mobility by deploying smart traffic lights that dynamically adjust signal timings based on real-time vehicle and cyclist mobile apps.

Reverse Engineering Dutch Intelligent Traffic Systems

Wesley Neelen and Rik van Duijn analyze intelligent traffic light controllers (iVRI) and companion mobile smartphone applications used across the Netherlands.

Forging GPS Telemetry and Priority Requests

Flaws in backend API authentication and a complete lack of cryptographic message signing allowed the researchers to forge cyclist approach signals, turning traffic lights green on demand.

Coordinated Disclosure and Urban Security Governance

The authors recount their disclosure process with Dutch government authorities and outline essential security requirements for connected public infrastructure.

talks.title: Whispers Among the Stars: Satellite Broadband Security
talks.teaser: Oxford researcher James Pavur uses a $300 home satellite TV dish to intercept sensitive enterprise and maritime broadband data transmitted unencrypted across outer space.
talks.summary:
The Explosive Growth of Satellite Broadband

Geostationary and low-Earth orbit satellites broadcast high-speed data downlinks over massive geographic footprints covering oceans, airspace, and continents.

Intercepting Ku-Band Feeds with Budget Television Hardware

James Pavur demonstrates that using a standard $300 consumer satellite dish, tuner card, and software-defined radio enables eavesdropping on gigabytes of live satellite traffic.

Harvesting Sensitive Enterprise, Aviation, and Maritime Data

Analyzing unencrypted DVB-S2 satellite streams exposed aircraft passengers' in-flight browsing, maritime ship telemetry, critical utility SCADA data, and corporate emails.

Practical Cryptographic Countermeasures for Satellite Networks

Pavur presents mitigation strategies, urging telecommunications satellite operators and enterprise customers to enforce end-to-end transport layer encryption.

talks.title: Discovering Hidden Properties to Attack Node.js Ecosystem
talks.teaser: Feng Xiao presents Hidden Property Abusing (HPA), a novel attack vector exploiting internal Node.js runtime properties to achieve arbitrary code execution.
talks.summary:
The Ubiquity of Node.js in Server and Desktop Applications

Node.js provides a cross-platform runtime for JavaScript, executing critical server-side APIs, cloud microservices, and desktop Electron applications.

Introducing Hidden Property Abusing (HPA)

Feng Xiao introduces Hidden Property Abusing (HPA), an attack technique that leverages internal, undocumented object properties and engine built-ins exposed by Node.js.

Manipulating Application Control Flow and Memory

By manipulating hidden properties in popular NPM frameworks, an attacker can alter runtime logic, bypass authentication checks, and chain execution gadgets to RCE.

Defending JavaScript Runtimes Against Property Manipulation

The author provides defensive coding patterns and automated scanning tools to detect hidden property exposure in open-source JavaScript codebases.

talks.title: Exploiting Key Space Vulnerabilities in the Physical World
talks.teaser: Bill Graydon applies information theory to physical master key systems, demonstrating how to mathematically reconstruct building master keys from partial key impressions.
talks.summary:
Information Theory in Physical Master Key Systems

Pin-tumbler master key systems rely on geometric key bittings to balance user access, but mathematical relationships between keys leak entropy about the system architecture.

Applying Entropy and Key Space Cryptanalysis

Bill Graydon demonstrates how comparing just a few employee office keys allows calculating the exact bitting parameters of the building master key without picking a single lock.

Impressioning and Decoding Pin Stacks

Combining physical lock impressioning techniques with information-theoretic reduction algorithms drastically reduces the search space needed to cut a functional master key.

Designing Secure Master Key Hierarchies

Graydon presents defensive key management guidelines and mathematical validation models for locksmiths and physical security engineers to eliminate key space leakage.

talks.title: Finding and Exploiting Bugs in Multiplayer Game Engines
talks.teaser: Jack Baker shares months of vulnerability research into Unreal Engine and Unity3D multiplayer networking protocols, exposing memory disclosure and speedhack bugs.
talks.summary:
The Attack Surface of Multiplayer Game Engines

Unreal Engine 4 and Unity3D power the vast majority of commercial multiplayer video games, implementing complex low-level C++ networking protocols over UDP.

Auditing Multiplayer Network Synchronization Protocols

Jack Baker examines the internal packet serialization and actor replication mechanisms used by major game engines to synchronize game state.

Discovering Memory Disclosures and Physics Manipulation

Fuzzing network protocol handlers uncovered critical memory disclosure flaws, remote denial of service vulnerabilities, and game state manipulation vectors.

Hardening Game Server Architectures

Baker outlines defensive engineering practices for game developers, emphasizing server-side authority validation and memory-safe packet parsing.

talks.title: Getting Shells on z/OS with Surrogat Chains (Encore)
talks.teaser: Jake Labelle presents advanced exploitation methodologies for IBM z/OS mainframes, mapping out complex RACF SURROGAT permission graphs to elevate to SPECIAL.
talks.summary:
Mainframe Identity and Access Complexity

IBM z/OS mainframes powering global financial infrastructure utilize intricate RACF authorization tables containing decades of accumulated user permissions.

Unraveling Multi-Step SURROGAT Class Delegations

Jake Labelle details how unprivileged user accounts can traverse nested batch job submission privileges to execute unauthorized JCL jobs as privileged IDs.

Constructing Automated Exploitation Graphs

Demonstrating automated scanning tools illustrates how red teams can ingest RACF database dumps to compute optimal escalation paths directly to mainframe root.

Auditing Mainframe Security Controls

System administrators are provided with practical remediation queries to prune orphaned SURROGAT profiles and harden z/OS access controls.

talks.title: How We Recovered $300,000 in Bitcoin from an Encrypted Zip File
talks.teaser: Cryptanalyst Michael Stay recovers $300,000 in locked Bitcoin keys by executing a sophisticated partial-known-plaintext cryptanalysis attack against legacy Zip encryption.
talks.summary:
The High-Stakes Recovery of Locked Crypto Assets

When a cryptocurrency investor forgot the password to an encrypted Zip archive containing hundreds of thousands of dollars in Bitcoin keys, they turned to legacy cryptanalysis.

Revisiting 20-Year-Old PKZIP Cryptanalysis

Michael Stay revisits Biham and Kocher’s classic known-plaintext attack against PKZIP stream encryption, adapting historical techniques to handle limited known plaintext.

Engineering GPU-Accelerated Key Reduction Engines

Stay outlines the mathematical breakthroughs and custom CUDA GPU kernels developed to reduce the internal CRC32 and linear feedback shift register state spaces.

Successfully Reconstructing the Private Key

Executing the cryptanalytic reduction recovered the internal encryption keys within days, unlocking the archive and securing the Bitcoin funds.

talks.title: Bytes in Disguise: Abusing Non-Volatile Memory
talks.teaser: Mickey Shkatov and Jesse Michael demonstrate abusing non-volatile memory chips in laptop trackpads and USB-C monitors to store stealthy malware payloads.
talks.summary:
The Hidden Nooks of Non-Volatile Memory

Modern computers contain dozens of independent non-volatile memory (NVM) chips across motherboards, trackpads, keyboards, and USB-C peripheral displays.

Auditing Auxiliary Peripheral Controllers

Mickey Shkatov and Jesse Michael investigate undocumented flash storage regions inside everyday laptop hardware components.

Achieving Persistence Without Triggering Side Effects

The authors demonstrate storing arbitrary data and executable code in unused peripheral flash memory, remaining completely undetected by host operating system antivirus tools.

Firmware Integrity Verification and Defenses

Mitigating NVM abuse requires implementing cryptographic firmware signing and hardware write-protect locking on all peripheral microcontrollers.

talks.title: Hacking the Hybrid Cloud
talks.teaser: Active Directory expert Sean Metcalf reveals attack paths bridging on-premises Windows networks and Azure Active Directory in hybrid enterprise clouds.
talks.summary:
The Insecurity of Hybrid Enterprise Deployments

Most global enterprises operate in hybrid environments, connecting legacy on-premises Active Directory forests to Azure AD and Microsoft 365 cloud services.

Attacking Synchronization and Trust Bridges

Sean Metcalf analyzes synchronization components like Azure AD Connect and Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS), uncovering critical trust subversion points.

Pivoting from On-Premises to Cloud Domination

Compromising an on-premises domain controller or synchronization server allows attackers to forge SAML tokens and assume Global Administrator rights in the cloud.

Hardening Hybrid Identity Architectures

Metcalf provides comprehensive architectural blueprints for securing tier-0 identity assets, isolating synchronization servers, and implementing robust conditional access policies.

talks.title: When TLS Hacks You
talks.teaser: Joshua Maddux weaponizes TLS protocol features—including session resumption and SNI parsing—to execute advanced Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks.
talks.summary:
Repurposing TLS Features as Attack Vectors

While TLS is designed to secure network communications, complex performance optimization features within the protocol can be weaponized by adversaries.

Weaponizing TLS for Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

Joshua Maddux demonstrates how manipulating TLS session tickets, SNI extensions, and client certificates enables bypassing SSRF URL filters and firewall protections.

Cross-Protocol Exploitation and Protocol Smuggling

By encapsulating plaintext protocol payloads inside encrypted TLS session resumptions, an attacker can coerce internal servers to interact with internal Redis or Memcached instances.

Securing Application TLS Implementations

The author provides guidance for application security engineers to enforce strict TLS client configurations and validate outgoing connection destinations.

talks.title: Demystifying Modern Windows Rootkits
talks.teaser: Bill Demirkapi demystifies writing modern Windows kernel rootkits, demonstrating novel kernel hooking techniques to manipulate user-mode network stacks.
talks.summary:
The Evolution of Windows Kernel Security

Modern Windows operating systems deploy Kernel Patch Protection (PatchGuard) and Driver Signature Enforcement (DSE) to prevent unauthorized kernel modification.

Building a Modern Windows Rootkit from Scratch

Bill Demirkapi walks through the complete lifecycle of kernel driver development, transitioning from a basic driver to an advanced stealth rootkit.

Novel Kernel Hooking and Network Stack Manipulation

Demirkapi reveals undocumented hooking primitives in kernel drivers to intercept and manipulate user-mode socket communications without triggering PatchGuard crashes.

Kernel-Mode vs. User-Mode Tradeoffs and Defenses

The presentation analyzes the operational drawbacks of kernel implants and outlines detection engineering strategies for security teams monitoring kernel telemetry.

talks.title: Pwn2Own Qualcomm Compute DSP for Fun and Profit
talks.teaser: Check Point researcher Slava Makkaveev audits Qualcomm Snapdragon compute DSPs (cDSP), disclosing critical vulnerabilities that allow malicious Android apps to take over the DSP.
talks.summary:
The Role of Compute DSPs in Snapdragon SoCs

Qualcomm Snapdragon chipsets integrate specialized Compute Digital Signal Processors (cDSP) to accelerate multimedia, audio processing, and machine learning at low power.

Auditing the Proprietary FastRPC and cDSP Subsystems

Slava Makkaveev investigates the closed-source FastRPC communication interface connecting the Android kernel to the Hexagon cDSP execution environment.

Discovering Multiple Zero-Days in DSP System Libraries

Fuzzing proprietary cDSP libraries and system calls uncovered severe memory corruption flaws allowing unprivileged Android applications to execute arbitrary code in DSP firmware.

Defending Low-Level Coprocessor Boundaries

Makkaveev presents exploit mitigations and details coordinated vulnerability fixes implemented by Qualcomm to secure DSP execution domains.

talks.title: A Hacker's Guide to Reducing Side Channel Attack Surfaces
talks.teaser: Google researcher Elie Bursztein combines deep learning side-channel attacks with AI explainability to pinpoint and remediate cryptographic hardware leakage.
talks.summary:
Deep Learning in Side-Channel Cryptanalysis

Deep learning models have revolutionized power and electromagnetic side-channel attacks, automating key extraction against hardware cryptographic implementations.

Applying AI Explainability to Hardware Leaks

Elie Bursztein demonstrates leveraging modern AI explainability techniques (such as Integrated Gradients and saliency maps) to inspect neural network activations.

Pinpointing Vulnerable Clock Cycles and Instructions

By visualizing which exact power trace timeframes the neural network utilizes to predict cryptographic key bits, engineers can instantly identify leaky code instructions.

Automating Hardware Defense and Hardening

Bursztein outlines automated testing pipelines for cryptographic developers to eliminate side-channel emissions before silicon fabrication.

talks.title: Reverse Engineering a Tesla Battery Management System for More Power
talks.teaser: Patrick Kiley reverse engineers the Tesla Model S Battery Management System (BMS), analyzing firmware changes that unlock 'Ludicrous Mode' acceleration.
talks.summary:
The Mechanics of Tesla's Ludicrous Mode

In 2015, Tesla introduced 'Ludicrous Mode' for the Model S P85D, upgrading the battery fuse and contactors to deliver 1500 amps and 2.8-second 0-60 acceleration.

Dissecting the Tesla Battery Management System (BMS)

Patrick Kiley performs an in-depth hardware and firmware teardown of the Tesla high-voltage battery pack and its internal microcontroller architecture.

Reverse Engineering CAN Bus Telemetry and Pyrofuse Logic

Analyzing CAN communications between the powertrain inverter and BMS reveals how the battery monitors current draw, cell temperatures, and pyrotechnic fuse status.

Unlocking High-Performance EV Capabilities

Kiley details firmware modification techniques and safety parameters for EV builders seeking to extract maximum power safely from salvaged battery packs.

talks.title: D0 N0 H4RM: Healthcare Security in a Pandemic
talks.teaser: Emergency physician Christian Dameff and a panel of experts examine escalating cyber threats to hospitals, patient safety, and medical devices during the COVID-19 pandemic.
talks.summary:
Healthcare Cyber Resiliency Under Pandemic Strain

As the COVID-19 pandemic overwhelmed emergency departments and intensive care units, ransomware operators intensified attacks against hospital clinical infrastructure.

The Direct Intersection of Cybersecurity and Patient Safety

Dr. Christian Dameff and clinical cybersecurity experts emphasize that medical device outages, EHR lockouts, and network downtime directly jeopardize human lives.

Vulnerabilities in Connected Clinical Equipment

Panelists review critical vulnerabilities in hospital networks—including bedside infusion pumps, ventilators, and laboratory telemetry systems.

A Call to Action for Hacker Defense

The session calls upon the global cybersecurity community to volunteer technical assistance, defend healthcare facilities, and prioritize medical device security research.

talks.title: DNSSECTION: A Practical Attack on DNS
talks.teaser: Hadrien Barral and Rémi Géraud-Stewart disclose DNSSECTION, demonstrating subtle structural attacks on DNS and DNSSEC record validation.
talks.summary:
The Expanding Complexity of the Domain Name System

Originally designed for simple hostname-to-IP resolution, DNS has evolved into a complex distributed database supporting DNSSEC, TXT metadata, and service discovery records.

Introducing the DNSSECTION Attack Framework

Hadrien Barral and Rémi Géraud-Stewart explore structural parsing ambiguities in how recursive resolvers process additional and authoritative record sections.

Exploiting Cache Inconsistencies and Resource Mappings

Manipulating record boundaries and DNSSEC cryptographic validation chains allows injecting unauthorized resource records into resolver caches.

Hardening Global DNS Infrastructure

The authors discuss protocol remediation strategies and release test suites for DNS server maintainers to prevent structural record pollution.

talks.title: After Stuxnet: Printing Still the Stairway to Heaven
talks.teaser: Peleg Hadar and Tomer Bar audit the Windows Print Spooler service a decade after Stuxnet, uncovering multiple zero-day SYSTEM privilege escalation bugs.
talks.summary:
The Persistent Legacy of Stuxnet's Print Spooler Exploit

In 2010, the Stuxnet worm weaponized a zero-day vulnerability in the Windows Print Spooler service to achieve SYSTEM-level code execution across industrial networks.

Revisiting the Print Spooler Attack Surface in 2020

SafeBreach researchers Peleg Hadar and Tomer Bar conduct a comprehensive audit of the modern Windows Print Spooler, expecting decades of hardening.

Discovering Multiple SYSTEM Privilege Escalation Zero-Days

Uncovering logic flaws in printer driver installation routines, directory junctions, and spool file handling enabled unprivileged local users to execute arbitrary code as SYSTEM.

Windows Architecture Hardening and Defensive Rules

The researchers discuss coordinated disclosure with Microsoft and provide endpoint detection telemetry to identify malicious spooler process injection.

talks.title: Practical VoIP/UC Hacking Using Mr. SIP
talks.teaser: Ismail Melih Tas and Kubilay Ahmet Kucuk introduce Mr. SIP, an advanced offensive VoIP auditing framework demonstrating novel SIP reflection and retransmission attacks.
talks.summary:
The Attack Surface of Enterprise VoIP and SIP Infrastructure

Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) underpins modern Voice over IP (VoIP) and Unified Communications (UC) deployments across enterprises and telecom service providers.

Introducing the Mr. SIP Offensive Security Toolkit

Ismail Melih Tas and Kubilay Ahmet Kucuk release Mr. SIP, a modular security framework for automated SIP network scanning, fuzzing, and penetration testing.

Novel SIP Retransmission and Reflection Attacks

The authors demonstrate novel attack primitives exploiting SIP message retransmission timers and transaction reflection logic to execute denial of service and user spoofing.

Securing Enterprise Voice Infrastructure

The presentation provides VoIP network administrators with configuration hardening checklists and intrusion detection signatures for anomalous SIP signaling.

talks.title: Hack Windows Machines with Printer Protocol
talks.teaser: Zhipeng Huo and Chuanda Ding uncover critical vulnerabilities in the Windows Print Spooler RPC protocol, achieving local privilege escalation and remote code execution.
talks.summary:
25 Years of the Windows Print Spooler Service

Executing as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM, the Windows Print Spooler service processes network requests, dynamic driver loading, and inter-process communication without process sandboxing.

Dissecting Spooler RPC Interfaces and Driver Loading

Zhipeng Huo and Chuanda Ding investigate undocumented RPC methods exposed by `spoolsv.exe`, evaluating how printer drivers are registered and verified.

Chaining Flaws from Local Privilege Escalation to Remote RCE

Exploiting path traversal and file manipulation flaws in driver installation pipelines allows unprivileged users to execute arbitrary code as SYSTEM locally and across the network.

Coordinated Remediation and Security Guidelines

The authors present exploit demonstrations and discuss Microsoft security patches designed to enforce strict signature validation on printer drivers.

talks.title: Hacking the Supply Chain: The Story of Ripple20
talks.teaser: JSOF researchers chronicle the discovery and coordinated disclosure of Ripple20, a series of critical vulnerabilities in a widely embedded TCP/IP stack affecting millions of IoT devices.
talks.summary:
Uncovering Systemic Flaws in Embedded TCP/IP Stacks

In 2020, JSOF researchers uncovered Ripple20, a set of 19 critical zero-day vulnerabilities in a proprietary TCP/IP software stack developed by Treck in the late 1990s.

The Hidden Proliferation of Supply Chain Code

Shlomi Oberman, Moshe Kol, and Ariel Schön trace how the vulnerable code was licensed, re-branded, and integrated into hundreds of millions of enterprise, medical, and industrial IoT devices.

Exploiting Remote Code Execution Across Diverse Hardware

Dissecting DNS, DHCP, and IPv6 packet parsing flaws illustrates achieving unauthenticated remote code execution on power grid controllers, smart printers, and patient monitors.

Coordinating a Multi-Vendor Global Disclosure

The speakers share the unprecedented 8-month global disclosure campaign involving CERT/CC, CISA, and hundreds of device manufacturers to coordinate patches.

talks.title: Applied Cash Eviction through ATM Exploitation
talks.teaser: Trey Keown and Brenda So reverse engineer automated teller machines, defeating firmware code signing and discovering network zero-days to jackpot ATMs remotely.
talks.summary:
The Stagnant State of Commercial ATM Security

Despite a decade of high-profile ATM jackpotting disclosures, legacy architectures and unverified peripheral middleware continue to plague retail ATMs.

Hardware Reverse Engineering and Firmware Emulation

Trey Keown and Brenda So restore physical JTAG interfaces, defeat firmware code signing, and construct custom bank host simulators to speak proprietary ATM transaction protocols.

Discovering Two Zero-Day Remote Exploits

The authors reveal a critical remote administration flaw granting unauthenticated root code execution, and a middleware vulnerability permitting remote network command injection.

Executing Remote Network Jackpotting

Live demonstrations illustrate how an attacker on the same banking network can command the physical cash dispenser to eject currency without physical machine tampering.

talks.title: Welcome to DEF CON Safe Mode and Badge Talk
talks.teaser: DEF CON founder The Dark Tangent welcomes the community to the first virtual DEF CON Safe Mode, followed by Lostboy detailing the mysteries of the DC Safe Mode badge.
talks.summary:
Transitioning DEF CON to a Global Virtual Event

In response to the global COVID-19 pandemic, DEF CON pivoted to DEF CON Safe Mode, uniting the worldwide hacker community online across Discord and Twitch.

Opening Remarks by The Dark Tangent

Conference founder Jeff Moss (The Dark Tangent) welcomes virtual attendees, reflecting on the resilience, ingenuity, and solidarity of the security research community.

The DEF CON Safe Mode Electronic Badge

Hardware designer Lostboy presents the artistic concept, cassette mixtape aesthetic, and hidden cryptographic puzzles engineered into the official Safe Mode electronic badge.

Engaging in Virtual Hacker Villages

The briefing guides participants through online capture-the-flag competitions, virtual villages, and interactive community sessions.

talks.title: Exploiting Key Space Vulnerabilities in the Physical World (Presentation)
talks.teaser: Bill Graydon demonstrates applying information theory and entropy reduction to derive physical building master keys from partial impressions.
talks.summary:
Information Theory in Physical Master Key Systems

Pin-tumbler master key systems rely on geometric key bittings to balance user access, but mathematical relationships between keys leak entropy about the system architecture.

Applying Entropy and Key Space Cryptanalysis

Bill Graydon demonstrates how comparing just a few employee office keys allows calculating the exact bitting parameters of the building master key without picking a single lock.

Impressioning and Decoding Pin Stacks

Combining physical lock impressioning techniques with information-theoretic reduction algorithms drastically reduces the search space needed to cut a functional master key.

Designing Secure Master Key Hierarchies

Graydon presents defensive key management guidelines and mathematical validation models for locksmiths and physical security engineers to eliminate key space leakage.
